newsitem.title: UK: AEA Technology sees continued growth in H2.
newsitem.headline: AEA Technology sees continued growth in H2.

text.p: Newly floated science and engineering firm AEA Technology Plc reported a 15 percent surge in underlying interim pretax profits on Monday and predicted the growth pattern would stretch into the second half.

But the headline profit figure was cut back to 1.1 million stg versus 5.3 million after accounting for the expected restructuring charge of more than five million pounds. Operating profit grew 18.4 percent to 6.4 million, a growth level which chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver sees continuing into the second part of the year.
"In the second half we expect a continuation of this performance, but the balance of our sales are skewed towards that part of the year," the chairman told Reuters.
He said in the interim statement "Trading remains in line with expectations and the group believes it shall continue to make significant progress in the second half."

The debut dividend payout for the group was 2.75 pence per share, with underlying earnings per share at 5.1 pence versus 4.5 pence. Cleaver told Reuters the profit surge, once charges were stripped out, was due to the company "focusing on cost efficiencies and moving the business in the right direction."
The group has shifted more of its business towards the private sector in the UK and overseas business and the chairman said he saw this proportion continuing to grow.

It already has interests in the Far East, notably Japan and in its results announced a clutch of new contracts including four million stg worth of business from drugs giant SmithKline Beecham to provide laboratory and waste mangement services.

It also reported that "We have gained a foothold in the fast-growing nuclear industry of China," winning a deal with the National Environmental Protection Agency to collaborate on radiological safety training and technology.

Looking at a breakdown of the results themselves, turnover is up 3.2 percent to 111.8 million as the group tries to shift its focus overseas and into the UK private sector (now accounting for 47 percent of turnover, up from 39 percent last year.)
New orders received rose 12.9 percent to 165.6 million. Technical products saw turnover up 21 percent to 24.5 million. Operating profits were up two million to 3.8 million.
Engineering services sales fell 12 percent to 31.4 million, reflecting an anticipated cut in business from the group's main customer UKAEA (UK Atomic Energy Authority).
Profits fell by 1.1 million to 1.5 million stg, reflecting the lower sales plus tighter margins.
Consultancy services turnover rose by 500,000 stg to 35.2 million, with profits a marginal 100,000 stg. The unit generates most of its profit in the second half, said the group.
Technical services sales rose 18 percent to 31.4 million, with profits up 300,000 stg to one million.

Commenting on the share performance since flotation, the chairman told Reuters ""Its obviously very pleasing that the market has looked on our shares as a good opportunity. We really didn't know how the market would respond."
AEA shares rose four pence to 391 1/2 pence on Monday. Since floating they have risen from the debut price of 323 pence on September 27.
